title: US street address in a sentence
text: Please send it to 4417 Larkspur Hollow Rd, Brookhaven, OR 97399 by Friday.

title: UK address with a flat number and a postcode
text: Deliver to Flat 3, 12 Quillon Road, Ashcombe Vale ZZ1 4QX.

title: Spanish address with floor, door and postal code
text: Dirección: Calle de los Tilos Altos 14, 3º B, 52990 Torrebruna.

title: postcode alone after a label
text: Postcode: ZZ1 4QX

title: place names in a sentence
text: We met in Torrebruna last week and again in Ashcombe Vale.
why: A place is found only from `known` or a detector the caller adds. Nothing in the core marks a capitalised word as a town.

title: recipient name under a ship-to label
text:
Ship to
Odalys Brenwick

Thank you for your order.

title: GPS coordinates
text: The pickup point is 41.0213, -31.4472 behind the shop.
why: No built-in detector looks for coordinates. Each half is a decimal number without a currency, which is not an amount.

title: card security code and expiry
text: Card ending 4242, CVV 381, expires 04/29.
why: A three-digit code is too short to be an id, `CVV` is not an id label, and a month and two-digit year is not a date to blind.

title: vehicle registration plate
text: The van was ZZ71 QXJ, parked outside.
why: No built-in detector looks for plates. With two digits it is too weak to be an id.

title: username after a label
text: Username: jpemberton42
why: No built-in detector looks for usernames or logins, `Username:` is not a label any detector reads, and with two digits the value is too weak to be an id.

title: username in a sentence
text: Log in as jpemberton with the usual password.
why: A lower-case login with no digits reads as an ordinary word to every pattern.

title: MAC address of a device
text: Device 02:5E:A1:3C:77:B9 joined the network.
why: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are typed ids, MAC addresses are not, and the colon-separated pairs are too short for the generic id pattern.

title: age of a patient
text: The patient, aged 47, lives alone above the bakery.
why: Ages, job titles and other details that identify someone only in combination are not a kind blind replaces.

title: name and town in a CSV row
text:
name,city
Odalys Brenwick,Torrebruna
why: Column and field names such as `name` or `city` are not used to find values, and a CSV row has no greeting, signature or label to start from.

title: SWIFT or BIC code
text: BIC: QXKRESMMXXX for the transfer.
why: No built-in detector looks for SWIFT or BIC codes. Eleven letters without a digit are not an id.

title: UK landline written with its leading 0
text: Call 020 7946 0958 after noon.
why: The phone patterns read a UK number with `+44` or `0044`, and a mobile with `07`, but not a landline written nationally.

title: Mexican phone layout
text: Llámame al (55) 1234-5678 por la tarde.
why: A two-digit area code in brackets followed by four and four digits matches none of the phone layouts.

title: French phone layout
text: Appelez le 01 99 00 41 27 demain.
why: Five pairs of digits match none of the phone layouts. Locales other than English and Spanish are not found.

title: German date
text: Termin am 7. April 2026 in der Praxis.
why: The date patterns read English and Spanish forms. A day with a full stop before the month is not one of them.

title: Swedish phone layout
text: Ring 08-465 004 27 före lunch.
why: An area code with a dash and groups of three digits matches none of the phone layouts. Locales other than English and Spanish are not found.

title: German phone layout
text: Rufen Sie (030) 123 45 67 an.
why: A bracketed area code with a leading 0 and groups of three, two and two digits matches none of the phone layouts.

title: French date
text: Rendez-vous le 7 avril 2026 au cabinet.
why: The date patterns read English and Spanish month names, not French ones.

title: name after a German title
text: Sehr geehrte Frau Brenwick, anbei die Rechnung.
why: The titles that mark a name are English and Spanish. `Frau`, `Herr`, `M.` and `Mme` are not among them.

title: street without a house number
text: She lives on Larkspur Hollow Rd near the school.
why: A street line needs a house number before its name. Without one, a name and a suffix read like any capitalised phrase.

title: German address layout
text: Lieferadresse: Tannenweg 12, 99998 Kleinhausen
why: The street patterns read English and Spanish layouts. A German street written as one word with the number after it is neither, and `Lieferadresse` is not a block label.

title: town, state and ZIP code in a sentence
text: Our office in Brookhaven, OR 97399 opens on Monday.
why: A town, region and postal code count after a street, on a line of their own or after a postal label. In a sentence with no street before them, the town's first word cannot be told from the words that open the sentence.

title: flat number on its own line above the street
text:
Flat 3
12 Quillon Road
Ashcombe Vale
ZZ1 4QX
why: The lines after a street line count as its locality. A unit on the line before it, outside a labelled block, is not read. The street, town and postcode are replaced.

title: town after a street, then the rest of the sentence
text: Please send it to 4417 Larkspur Hollow Rd, Brookhaven by Friday.
why: A town alone after a street counts only up to a comma, a stop or the end of its line. Followed by more of the sentence, its words cannot be told from the start of a new clause (`Rd, Please call`). The street is replaced.

title: town alone on the line below a street
text:
4417 Larkspur Hollow Rd
Brookhaven
why: Outside a labelled block, a line below a street counts when it holds a postal code, or is a town with a postal code line after it. A capitalised line alone could be the next sentence, so it is not read. The street is replaced.

title: long note above a lower-case street in a block
text:
Ship to
Please leave the parcel with the neighbour at the back door
4417 larkspur hollow rd
why: A block passes over up to two lines of six words or fewer above the street. A longer line ends it, so a sentence below a label is not read as an address, and a street in lower case is found only inside a block.
